message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo align to abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is either AAA or prevalent AAA). Several are framework/portability-style outputs (PGS001784 from a global-biobank lessons paper; PGS002054 from a UKB portability sweep), which domain guidance says should generally not outrank a disease-focused multi-cohort AAA score unless they have clearly stronger endpoint/metric evidence. PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with multi-cohort development, supporting disease-focused relevance; among them, PGS003972 shows a clean direct AAA phenotype and avoids the unusually high full-model-like C-index (0.882) seen for PGS003973 that may be largely covariate-driven given only basic age/sex covariates are listed but no PRS-only/incremental metrics are provided. However, the evidence remains limited/conflicted because most candidates lack comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2, some report only full-model metrics (AUC/C-index), and covariates are unknown for multiple models; this prevents a clearly high-confidence best choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO, and their phenotyping_reported is generally aligned (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Several reported discrimination metrics appear to be full-model (e.g., AUROC/C-index) rather than PRS-only, making cross-model comparison uncertain; only PGS001784 provides an explicit PRS-only R2 (0.014661), while others provide partial-r or full-model AUROC/C-index, and PGS000753 reports only an OR per SD (1.37). In line with the domain policy to avoid letting a generic framework/portability score win on metric availability alone, I down-rank PGS001784 (global biobank framework) and PGS002054 (UKB portability framework). Between the remaining disease-focused candidates, PGS003972 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis context; PRS-CS; large multi-cohort development list) is preferred over PGS000753 (older, very sparse 29-variant P+T prevalent endpoint) and over PGS003429 (screening/cost-effectiveness framing; unknown covariates; only full-model AUROC/R2 shown). However, confidence remains low because PGS003972’s reported AUROC (0.69) is full-model/unspecified PRS isolation and covariates are unknown, while the sibling PGS003973 shows a much higher C-index (0.882) but also reflects a different modeling/validation setup, and the catalog metadata do not provide PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics to clearly identify the best-performing standalone PRS."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Several candidates come from framework/portability-style papers (PGS001784: global biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability of 245 scores), which domain guidance down-ranks when disease-focused alternatives exist. PGS003429 is embedded in a screening/cost-effectiveness context and reports only full-model AUROC (0.708) with unknown covariates, making PRS contribution hard to compare. PGS003972/PGS003973 are from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) but only report full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.69; C-index 0.882) with limited PRS-only isolation; the very high C-index could be largely covariate-driven (age/sex) per domain guidance, and no incremental/PGS-only metrics are shown. PGS000753 (MVP-focused AAA genetics paper) provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, European validation) with basic covariates and avoids risk-wrapper packaging; however, it is sparse (29 variants) and lacks explicit AUROC/R2, so the evidence does not support a high-confidence best choice over the newer meta-analysis scores. Therefore, select PGS000753 as the best-supported non-framework, endpoint-faithful option, but rate overall as sub-optimal due to missing PRS-comparable metrics and unresolved comparability across candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo, with generally aligned endpoints (mostly ‘abdominal aortic aneurysm’; one is explicitly ‘prevalent’). Several candidates come from framework/portability-style publications (PGS001784: ‘Global Biobank analyses…’; PGS002054: ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’) which domain guidance says should be down-ranked when a disease-focused alternative exists. PGS003429 is from a screening cost-effectiveness paper and reports only full-model AUROC/R² with unknown covariates, making the discrimination evidence hard to compare. PGS003972/PGS003973 are from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) but only provide full-model AUROC/C-index (no PRS-only/incremental metric shown here), so their apparently high C-index (0.882) cannot be treated as PRS-comparable in this context. PGS000753 (MVP AAA paper, Circulation) is disease-focused, uses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) in European validation, and avoids the framework/packaging concerns; however, it is sparse (29 variants), uses a prevalent phenotype, and lacks AUC/R² in the provided metadata, so the selection remains sub-optimal with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have acceptable endpoint alignment (diagnosis-style abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent). Two candidates (PGS002054, PGS001784) come from framework/portability-style publications (UKB portability; global biobank lessons) and one (PGS003429) is a screening cost-effectiveness paper; domain guidance advises not to let such framework/packaging contexts outrank disease-focused scores unless they have clearly superior, PRS-comparable evidence. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program) with clear phenotype (“Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and reports an interpretable per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) in a substantial validation sample (n=46,564), providing direct PRS signal evidence even though AUROC/R2 are missing. Competing disease-focused/meta-analysis options (PGS003972/PGS003973) report only full-model discrimination metrics (AUROC/C-index) with limited PRS-isolated reporting and one shows an unusually high C-index (0.882) that may be largely covariate-driven per the provided policy, while covariates are unknown/variable across those records. Because key comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) are largely absent across candidates and several reported discriminations are likely full-model, the selection remains sub-optimal and confidence is not high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping (\"abdominal aortic aneurysm\"; one is explicitly prevalent). Two are from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; PGS003972/PGS003973) with multi-cohort development and basic/unknown covariates, which domain guidance prefers over pan-trait/framework or portability-style scores when available. Between those two, PGS003972 is favored because it has a slightly broader, more externally oriented cohort list in training/development (includes UKB and VIVA in addition to the shared multi-cohort set) and has multiple validation records (record_count=3) rather than a single record, providing somewhat more internal corroboration in the visible metadata. Confidence is limited because the available discrimination metrics are not PRS-comparable across models: several report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., 0.69 for PGS003972; 0.882 C-index for PGS003973; 0.868 for the Global Biobank framework), and only one (PGS001784) reports a covariates-regressed-out R2 (~0.0147), so direct PRS-only performance comparisons remain ambiguous."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping (abdominal aortic aneurysm; PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis in Nat Genet with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance prefers over framework/portability-style scores when endpoints are similarly aligned. Between those two, PGS003972 provides an AUROC (0.69) without obvious covariate inflation signals (covariates listed as unknown, but no heavy clinical covariates are disclosed), while PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) that is likely dominated by basic age/sex covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) and is not an explicitly PRS-only metric; therefore its apparent advantage is not comparable as PRS discrimination. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have acceptable endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported is AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (\"abdominal aortic aneurysm\"; one is prevalent AAA). Among disease-focused candidates, the Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis family (PGS003972/PGS003973) provides the most disease-focused multi-cohort development context; between them, PGS003972 is selected because it has broader supporting validation evidence in the catalog (record_count=3 vs 1) with the same direct AAA phenotype and similar study context, while the very high C-index reported for PGS003973 (0.882) is likely dominated by basic covariates (Age/Age^2/Sex) and lacks PRS-only isolation.
